title: Spot phase changes dominate the within-sector relative phase residuals in 118 TESS complex periodic variables
abstract: We test which measured phase clock contributes to dip-minus-spot changes in released TESS measurements of 118 complex periodic variables, with 377 single-sector visits. We reproduce the reported relative slope coefficient of 1.060 x 10^-5 cycles squared per day. Setting dip phase to a constant while keeping the measured spot phase gives 7.43 x 10^-6, a coefficient ratio of 0.70 (95% star bootstrap interval 0.54 to 0.99). After a separate affine trend is removed from each clock, the typical spot-to-dip residual variance ratio is 19.0 (13.6 to 23.9). The typical correlation of spot residual with relative residual is -0.976. The result holds with stricter quality cuts and with each star removed in turn. Small dip-pattern changes remain. The relative coefficient cannot by itself identify a material diffusion rate. The audit uses released template shifts and does not refit raw photometry, identify the stellar rotation phase, or test long-gap phase memory. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and an external-scratch reproduction script are supplied.

display.caption: Left: star-level spot-to-dip residual variance ratio after affine trends are removed. Centre: correlation of spot and relative residuals. Right: the same slope-based coefficient fitted to each phase clock. CPVs are blue; zero-offset fixed-dip injections are orange. A large relative coefficient does not isolate dip motion.

citations.reason: Uses verified released chunk shifts; reproduces the relative slope coefficient but challenges its attribution to material motion through a fixed-dip counterfactual and a separate covariance audit.
Upstream CPV selection inherited through the phase measurement publication.
